stories.title: The First People Long Ago
stories.teaser: Imagine a world with no houses, no shops, and no roads, just open skies, wild animals and tall trees. That’s where the very first people lived. How did they stay warm, safe, and fed?
learning_objectives: Early humans lived thousands of years ago
Early humans used simple stone tools
Fire helped humans stay warm and cook food
Early humans hunted and gathered food
People once lived in caves or simple shelters

pages.text: Long before cities and roads, the first people lived close to nature under wide open skies.
pages.image_prompt: Flat pastel illustration of early humans in natural landscape with hills and trees, simple shapes, soft colors, non-scary, 1:1 aspect ratio.

pages.text: They did not have houses like ours. Some families stayed in caves or built simple shelters from branches.
pages.image_prompt: Flat pastel illustration of early humans near cave and simple branch shelter, gentle and educational, 1:1 aspect ratio.

pages.text: To find food, they gathered fruits, nuts, and roots from the land.
pages.image_prompt: Flat pastel illustration of early humans collecting berries and plants, calm and friendly style, 1:1 aspect ratio.

pages.text: Sometimes they worked together to hunt animals for meat and clothing.
pages.image_prompt: Flat pastel non-scary illustration of early humans cooperating in simple hunt scene, educational tone, 1:1 aspect ratio.

pages.text: They shaped sharp stones into tools. Stone tools helped them cut, dig, and build.
pages.image_prompt: Flat pastel illustration of stone tools with simple arrows showing use, educational toddler style, 1:1 aspect ratio.

pages.text: One of the biggest discoveries was fire. Fire gave warmth and light at night.
pages.image_prompt: Flat pastel illustration of early humans sitting safely around small campfire, warm soft colors, 1:1 aspect ratio.

pages.text: Fire also helped cook food, making it easier to chew and digest.
pages.image_prompt: Flat pastel illustration of simple cooking over fire, friendly and calm, 1:1 aspect ratio.

pages.text: Over time, people learned new skills and passed knowledge to children.
pages.image_prompt: Flat pastel illustration of adult teaching child to shape stone tool, gentle educational scene, 1:1 aspect ratio.

pages.text: These early humans slowly traveled across continents, spreading to many parts of the world.
pages.image_prompt: Flat pastel world map with simple dotted path showing early migration, soft colors, 1:1 aspect ratio.

pages.text: From simple shelters and stone tools, human history began its long journey.
pages.image_prompt: Flat pastel sunrise over ancient landscape with early humans walking forward, hopeful tone, 1:1 aspect ratio.

stories.title: The Story of Money and Trade
stories.teaser: Long ago, if you wanted some apples, you might have to trade a clay pot for them! How did people go from swapping things to tapping a card or a phone to pay?

Paper money replaced heavy coins
Banks help keep money safe
Today digital payments are common
